criteria.criterion: A fake-host test (run with cargo test -p athena-core) shows land_pr, with the early head's CI run still in progress, polling ci_runs on the early commit and pushing the landing commit only after the run reports completed.
criteria.evidence: land_pr_waits_for_the_early_run_before_pushing passed. It checks the exact event log: [ci_runs early1, sleep 20, ci_runs early1, sleep 20, ci_runs early1, replace], the warning 'waited 40s … completed', and that the PR ends up Landed.

criteria.criterion: A fake-host test shows that when the early run is already completed, the landing push happens at once with no sleep calls.
criteria.evidence: land_pr_pushes_at_once_when_the_early_run_is_completed passed. The log is exactly [ci_runs early1, replace] with no sleep, and the note says 'waited 0s … already completed'.

criteria.criterion: A test shows that when the run never completes within the bounded wait, the landing commit is still pushed, and that the wait is bounded (default about 10 minutes, injectable so the test needs no real sleeping).
criteria.evidence: land_pr_pushes_anyway_when_the_early_run_never_completes passed. With a 60s limit it records three 20s sleeps on the fake sleep, then the replace. The note says 'waited 60s … timed out', merge is called with landing1, and it checks the default early_run_wait() is 600s.

criteria.criterion: A test shows that a failed (or timed-out) early run, and an early commit with no runs or a ci_runs error, change nothing about merging: land pushes and merges exactly as before and the full landing run decides.
criteria.evidence: land_pr_early_run_failure_changes_nothing passed. It covers four cases: failure, timed_out, no runs, and a ci_runs error. In each the log is [ci_runs early1, replace] with no sleep, merge is called with landing1, and merge_requested, link, checks and reruns match the baseline run.

criteria.criterion: cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets are clean, and cargo fmt --check passes; existing land_pr and publish tests still pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's records show fmt, clippy and `cargo test --locked` (1222 tests) passed. I re-ran the land_pr tests: all 9 that existed before the change still pass, unchanged.

criteria.criterion: The wait applies only when an early head exists and differs from the landing commit; the wait is logged or reported in a way a reader can see how long it waited and why it stopped.
criteria.evidence: In the diff, wait_for_early_run is called only from replace_early. That is reached only when an early head exists, equals the remote head, and differs from the landing commit, both in land_pr and in publish. Its note, 'waited Ns for the early run of <sha>…: <reason>', is added to report.warnings. land_pr_reports_why_the_early_wait_stopped_only_when_there_is_an_early_head passed: with no early head, or an early head equal to the landing commit, ci_runs is never called and no note is added.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for this change that says the next real landing's time is still to be measured. It must not state an invented number. The measured time is recorded only once a real landing has been observed, with its source (for example the PR number and the run timestamps).
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The entry cites only the PR #180 timestamps given in the request. It says 'The landing time after this change is still to be measured: it is recorded here, with its PR number and run timestamps, once a real landing has been observed.' No new number is given.

findings.summary: The wait covers all of the early commit's workflow runs, not only the 'fmt, clippy, tests' run.
findings.evidence: It requires runs.iter().all(status == completed). A slow unrelated workflow could keep the wait going until the limit. The wait is still bounded, and the CHANGELOG mentions this.

findings.summary: land.rs, run.rs and test_support.rs were planned deliverables but were not changed.
findings.evidence: git diff HEAD~1 --stat lists only CHANGELOG.md and gh.rs. Every criterion is still shown, and the reading expected land.rs to stay as it was.

summary: The change passes. Before land swaps the early-pushed head for the landing commit, it now checks the early commit's CI runs every 20 seconds, for at most 600 seconds by default. Tests can set a different limit through PrHost::early_run_wait. It pushes as soon as the runs finish. It also pushes when the limit runs out, when a run failed, when there are no runs, or when the host's reply can't be read. Each time it adds a warning line saying how many seconds it waited and why it stopped. The new tests fail without the wait: the order test checks the event log step by step. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core land_pr_` and all 14 tests passed, the 5 new ones and the 9 that were already there. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs all passed. The CHANGELOG entry describes the PR #180 race and says the next landing's time is still to be measured, with no made-up number. Only gh.rs and CHANGELOG.md changed. land.rs, run.rs and test_support.rs were planned but untouched, and nothing that was needed is missing because of that. One small gap: the wait covers all of a commit's workflow runs, not just the 'fmt, clippy, tests' run, because the host's reply doesn't include workflow names. The CHANGELOG says so.
